title: Optimizing Legal Document Retrieval for Boutique Firms
business: Boutique law firms managing thousands of case files and historical precedents.
problem: High latency and storage costs when performing semantic searches across massive, unstructured document repositories using standard high-dimensional embeddings.
solution: Utilizing nomic-embed-text-v1.5 with Matryoshka Representation Learning to compress embedding vectors while maintaining semantic retrieval accuracy for RAG applications.
steps: Prepend the search_document prefix to all historical legal case files before embedding.
Generate embeddings for the document corpus using the Sentence Transformers library.
Apply layer normalization and slice the resulting vectors to a smaller dimensionality, such as 256, to reduce storage footprint.
Prepend the search_query prefix to incoming attorney questions before performing vector similarity searches.
outcome: Reduced memory overhead for the vector database and faster retrieval times with minimal impact on the relevance of retrieved legal precedents.
limitation: Reducing the embedding dimensionality via Matryoshka Representation Learning involves a tradeoff where smaller vector sizes lead to a slight reduction in overall retrieval performance; developers should validate accuracy against their specific dataset after compression.

code.content:
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
import torch.nn.functional as F

# Initialize model
model = SentenceTransformer("nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5")

# Embed document with prefix
doc = ['search_document: Case precedent regarding liability...']
embeddings = model.encode(doc, convert_to_tensor=True)

# Apply Matryoshka compression to 256 dimensions
embeddings = F.layer_norm(embeddings, normalized_shape=(embeddings.shape[1],))
compressed_embeddings = embeddings[:, :256]
compressed_embeddings = F.normalize(compressed_embeddings, p=2, dim=1)
code.explanation: This code demonstrates how to prepare a document for the index using the required prefix and how to compress the resulting embedding to 256 dimensions to save space.
